pairs.difference: B: the yellow-gold star sits on magenta rings. There are only two hue masses, and the silver studs are the only rest. Warm share 0.996 and 1.94 hue families are both outside the real range. A: the red and yellow umbrella on cyan is a true warm/cool split with a lilac pole, and its shadow panels stay rich red (1.077 kept).
pairs.fix: Put the gold star on a cooler teal or blue background, keep the studs a cool neutral grey, and let the star's shaded side deepen toward olive-gold rather than orange.

pairs.difference: A: the rust-brown boot on a blue diamond pattern keeps a believable leather colour, with a grey spur and cream stitching. B: the navy cap with a gold band on cyan is cool on cool with one warm accent. Each misses a real-range edge only by a hair (A shadow 0.717, B warm share 0.049), and neither shows a colour fault the lessons point to.

B: the teal background is dark and dull at the corners, and its chroma of 0.0918 is below every real card. The hat is a single orange-brown mass against it. A: the beige jacket with orange cuffs and a dark green sash on bright green has a neutral rest area and a background inside the real range, though its cream leans warm.
pairs.fix: Make the background a brighter, cleaner teal with lighter rays and no dark muddy corners. Keep the hat brown, with a darker band as the only second tone.

pairs.difference: B: the signs, post and their shadows are all one saturated orange, so the wood has lost its brown local colour, and only the pink butterfly breaks it. Background chroma of 0.1062 is below the real range. A: the phone box is a believable pillar-box red on green with a grey phone and dark plinth as neutrals. It is loud (subject 0.1545, at the real ceiling), but the red is the object's own colour.
pairs.fix: Paint the signpost as weathered mid-brown wood with greyer plank edges and cool brown shadows, not bright orange. Keep the sky a clear, even blue.

pairs.difference: A: lime cactus, pink stripes and orange sand are all equally loud, with no neutral to rest the eye. The cactus reads as one flat lime mass, and subject chroma of 0.1641 is at the real ceiling. B: the blue racket on court green has a pale line, a black grip and rich teal-navy shadows. B's weak point is numeric: warm share 0.01 and 2.48 hue families fall below the real range.
pairs.fix: Make the cactus a deeper, duller sage green with blue-green shadows, soften the sand to a muted tan, and quiet the pink background so that only the flower stays bright.

pairs.difference: B: orange barrel, orange floor and pale yellow wall pull the whole card warm (0.968, above the real ceiling), and the shadows are orange-brown everywhere. The iron bands are the only cooler note. A: the orange suitcase has a green floor and stickers in blue, red and green, giving 4.02 hue families and a real warm/cool break.
pairs.fix: Make the barrel a darker, natural brown oak with grey steel hoops, change the wall to a cool pale blue or mint, make the floor a greyer wood, and shift shadows toward cool brown.

pairs.difference: B: neon green, teal, magenta and orange laces and trims all sit at pure hue on a blue shoe, giving 5.49 hue families, above the real range. The whites go lilac-pink, and the card has too many accents competing. A: one blue kettle on coral with a muted grey-brown rock gives two clear hue roles and a natural neutral, though its 2.11 hue families and 0.1263 background are slightly low.
pairs.fix: Limit the sneakers to blue with white soles and one accent colour. Remove the rainbow trims and make the laces plain white.

pairs.difference: B: tan paper, olive wall and grey planks form a very quiet card. Background chroma of 0.0488 is about half the real minimum, and 2.47 hue families and 0.612 shadow kept are also low. Shadows fall to dead grey-brown. A: the orange locker on violet has a clear complementary hero/background split, a blue shoe accent and a background within the real range.
pairs.fix: Replace the olive wall and grey boards with a bright, clean coloured background such as turquoise or red, and shade the parchment with richer caramel instead of grey-green.

pairs.difference: A: walls, ground, sky and distant buildings all share one peach-orange cast, with warm share 0.976 and only 1.86 hue families, far outside the real range. Only small blue windows and red trim break it. B: the orange post and red ring on turquoise water have a strong warm/cool split and 6.34 hue families, though its dark post shadows lose chroma (0.543).
pairs.fix: Change the sky to clear pale blue and the ground to a cooler, sandy beige. Paint the saloon in a mid-brown wood with grey-blue shadows, keeping the red only on the trim.

pairs.difference: A: the canvas is creamy, and wood, dirt, grass and wheels all pull orange-red, with warm share 0.755 above the real ceiling. The lens shows cream and rust spreading over most of the wagon, matching the warm cream cast of the generated lessons. B: orange boat on cyan water has green lily pads, an inside-range warm share of 0.471 and a clear split.
pairs.fix: Make the canvas a cooler off-white with soft blue-grey folds, turn the dirt road to a duller grey-tan, and keep the wagon wood a natural brown.

pairs.difference: A: pink-purple sky and orange desert wash the whole card, so the metal blades and tank pick up pink and tan. Background chroma of 0.1518 and warm share of 0.722 are both above the real range. B: the blue door, green ivy and orange frame are three clear local colours inside the range, with a cream wall and flowers as accents.
pairs.fix: Use a clear blue daytime sky with a sandy tan ground, and keep the metal blades and tank a cool neutral grey without any pink or orange tint.

pairs.difference: B: a saturated violet background of 0.2397 is above the real ceiling and louder than the fins. The card has 1.67 hue families and a warm share of 0.146, both below the range, with only yellow against purple. A: the green car has a grey-blue floor, white stripe and orange backdrop, giving many neutrals and 5.38 hue families. Its dark bumper does drop shadow chroma to 0.343.
pairs.fix: Quiet the purple background to a softer, lighter violet with a calm pale centre, and give the fins a second cooler colour such as a blue foot pocket.

pattern: Generated cards give themselves away through colour casts across the whole card: one warm hue over everything (p09, p06, p10, p11), or a single hero/background pair with too few hue families (p01, p12). Shared cream and orange in neutrals and wood replace the cooler greys, blue-lilac shadows and browner local colours seen on the real lesson cards. Many calls are low confidence because several pairs are close on colour alone. The folder name and subjects suggest western-themed props may be the generated ones; that hint was not used, and p02 and p07 go against it.
